description:
Prices a swap between two different tokens across the indexed venues and stores it under a `quoteId`.

- **Cost:** 0.01 USDC per call, paid over x402.
- **Inputs:** `sell`, `buy` and `amount` (required), and optional `side`, `slippageBps`, split and hop limits, `venues`, `excludeVenues`, `taker` and `ttlSec`. Name the wallet that will trade in `taker` to get `readiness`.
- **Returns:** the best plan in `best`, with `routes`, `safety`, `warnings` and `expiresAt`. With `taker`, `readiness` says whether that wallet holds the input, which approval `tradeSwap` will need, whether it can pay gas and the swap fee, and the total cost to finish. The `quoteId` is good until `expiresAt` (`ttlSec`, at most 120 seconds). Check `safety.verdict` before you swap.
- **Errors:**
  - 400 `ticker_not_allowed`: `sell` and `buy` are 0x addresses. Resolve a ticker with `tradeSearch`.
  - 400 `unsupported_pair`: `sell` and `buy` must be different assets.
  - 400 `unknown_venue`: use ids from `tradeVenues`.
  - 404 `token_not_found`: no ERC-20 token at that address.
  - 422 `no_route`, `insufficient_liquidity`, `unsupported_venue` or `buy_reverts`: no tradable route. Stop, or change the trade.
- **Next:**
  - `tradeSwap`: turn the `quoteId` into unsigned transactions. Do it when `next` is `swap`. `stop` means the quote cannot be traded, and `nextReason` says why: `best.executable` is false, the verdict is `cannot_sell`, `high_tax` or `illiquid`, `readiness.ready` is false, the request asked `exitRisk` `stop` and the token you buy rated high (`nextReason.code` `exit_risk_high`; `tradeSwap` refuses it with 422), or the sell check was `inconclusive` because of the token or an unknown cause (`nextReason.code` `sell_unverified`; `tradeSwap` refuses it with 422, including for a sale into USDC). `requote` means the sell check was `inconclusive` because it did not finish (a provider error, the call budget, the simulation allowance): quote again shortly, and stop if the second quote also answers `requote`. While the server's simulation budget is paused, a quote whose sell check needs a simulation answers 503 `rpc_unavailable` instead, and nothing is charged; a retry within minutes meets the same pause. `tradeSwap` still accepts a `requote` quote: on a token output it re-checks the sell from the recipient wallet, serves the swap if that check passes, and answers 503 `rpc_unavailable` if the re-check does not finish; on a USDC or pinned output it serves the swap, because the swap's own simulation is the exit. An `inconclusive` quote is still charged. A sell tax above 1000 basis points (`trade.quote.max_sell_tax_bps`) is a `high_tax` verdict: the sell works, the tax is too high to trade (`nextReason.code` `high_tax`; `tradeSwap` refuses it with 422). A sell tax at or above 9000 basis points (`trade.quote.honeypot_sell_tax_bps`) is a `cannot_sell` verdict, a honeypot. A tax measured inside the launchpad's launch window reads `high_tax` with a `launch_window` warning instead, and the check after the window settles it. `exitRisk` on the response is the stored exit-risk rating of the token you buy, null when you buy USDC or the token has no rating yet. It is separate from the sell-check verdict: it says whether outside buyers got out, from the trading history. A high level adds an `exit_risk_high` warning. The request's `exitRisk` policy is `warn` by default and leaves `next` alone; `stop` answers `next: stop` on a high level, and only for the token you buy, so it never blocks selling a token to USDC.

Costs 10000 base units (0.01 USDC) per call. Or send an account's key in the ARCGATE-KEY header on the MCP connection to pay in units instead. Payment goes in params._meta["x402/payment"]; use an x402-aware MCP client (see https://docs.arcgate.dev/#arcgate/description/mcp-for-agents).

allowSplits.description: Whether the trade may be split across several paths.

amount.description: A positive decimal string in the token's own units, e.g. "1.5" for 1.5 USDC, not base units. It is the `sell` amount for `exactIn` and the `buy` amount for `exactOut`.

buy.description: The token to buy, as a 0x address. Native and ERC-20 USDC are the same asset. It must differ from `sell`; either side may be USDC.

excludeVenues.description: Venue ids, from tradeVenues, to leave out.

exitRisk.description: What a high exit risk on the token you buy does (default `warn`). `warn` adds an `exit_risk_high` warning and leaves `next` as it is. `stop` answers `next: stop` with `nextReason.code` `exit_risk_high`, and POST /trade/v1/swap refuses the quote with 422 `exit_risk_high`. Exit risk is not the sell-check verdict. Only the token you buy counts, so `stop` never blocks selling a token to USDC.

maxHops.description: The most pools one path may cross (default 2).

maxSplits.description: The most paths one trade may be split across (default 3).

sell.description: The token to sell, as a 0x address (a ticker is `ticker_not_allowed`: resolve it with tradeSearch). Native and ERC-20 USDC are the same asset. It must differ from `buy`.

side.description: `exactIn` spends exactly `amount` of `sell`. `exactOut` buys exactly `amount` of `buy`.

slippageBps.description: How far the result may miss the quote, in basis points (default 100). It sets `minAmountOut` for `exactIn` and `maxAmountIn` for `exactOut`.

sources.description: Where routes come from. The default `native` is arcgate's own indexed venues. Any other source needs `taker`.

taker.description: The wallet that will trade, as a 0x address. Name it to get `readiness` back for that wallet.

ttlSec.description: How long the stored quote (and this response's expiresAt) stays live, in seconds (1-120, default 120). A caller may shorten it to re-quote sooner; it can never lengthen past 120s. Safe to shorten or leave at default: POST /trade/v1/swap always re-quotes and re-simulates at the current block and 409s quote_stale below the stored minAmountOut, so this bounds staleness risk, not price risk. The on-chain execution deadline is a separate parameter (deadlineSec, POST /trade/v1/swap).

venues.description: Quote only through these venue ids, from tradeVenues. Null allows every venue.

name: tradeQuote
